# Daily AI Thread (AI News Briefing)

> A free daily AI news briefing published every morning at 08:00 KST, in Korean and English as separate pages. Ten stories are selected from 12 RSS feeds, each read in full and summarized with a separate judgment about why it matters, plus one cross-cutting synthesis of the day.

## Current scale

- Published 17 days so far, starting 2026-07-23 without a gap
- 165 articles summarized
- 78 glossary entries
- 11 topics

## What this site is

- Independent, one-person project. No advertising, no sponsored placement, no affiliate links, no paid tier.
- Every article is read in full before it is summarized. RSS excerpts are not passed along; when an original cannot be read, the slot is swapped for a reserve candidate, and if none is available the edition simply runs shorter than ten.
- Each item is split into two blocks that must not be conflated: a Summary carrying only what the original reports, and a 'why it matters' block that is this site's own judgment.
- Written for people who need to keep up with AI because of their work — following context in a meeting, reporting upward, evaluating adoption — rather than for people who build AI systems.

## How the ten are selected

- Candidates come from 12 RSS feeds: industry press, official lab announcements, technical outlets, Korean media, and community signal.
- Ranking is a single score: source weight + cross-outlet corroboration (capped) + recency. At most three stories per source; official first-party announcements are guaranteed at least two slots.
- When several outlets cover the same event, only one runs and the others are linked beneath it. Links already published in a past edition are never selected again.
- The full funnel — how many items were scanned, where they were filtered out, and how many ran — is published every day on the data page.

## Citation

- Sharing links internally and quoting the summaries and analysis is explicitly allowed; no permission request is needed.
- When citing, credit "AI News Briefing (dailyaithread.com)" and link the specific dated page so readers can reach the original reporting.
- Copyright in each underlying article belongs to its publisher. This site carries only its own summaries and analysis, never the full text of a source article.

## Key pages

- [Today's briefing](https://www.dailyaithread.com/) | [English](https://www.dailyaithread.com/en): the current edition, replaced every morning
- [Archive index](https://www.dailyaithread.com/archive) | [English](https://www.dailyaithread.com/en/archive): every past edition, permanent per-date URLs
- [Data](https://www.dailyaithread.com/data) | [English](https://www.dailyaithread.com/en/data): what was scanned and what ran, published daily
- [Glossary](https://www.dailyaithread.com/glossary) | [English](https://www.dailyaithread.com/en/glossary): every term explained on the day it appeared
- [Topics](https://www.dailyaithread.com/topics) | [English](https://www.dailyaithread.com/en/topics): articles grouped by subject
- [Story timelines](https://www.dailyaithread.com/stories) | [English](https://www.dailyaithread.com/en/stories): events that unfolded over several days
- [About](https://www.dailyaithread.com/about) | [English](https://www.dailyaithread.com/en/about): method, limits, independence, and citation policy
- [RSS (Korean)](https://www.dailyaithread.com/feed.xml) | [RSS (English)](https://www.dailyaithread.com/en/feed.xml)

- [OpenAI's model breach of Hugging Face](https://www.dailyaithread.com/story/openai-hugging-face-breach) | [English](https://www.dailyaithread.com/en/story/openai-hugging-face-breach)

## Notes

Archive pages keep permanent per-date URLs and are never removed. Raw JSON under /archive/*.json is disallowed in robots.txt; use the HTML pages.
